key_insight: An automated, guideline-based evaluation pipeline enables broad testing of medical AI, while a small physician study found higher guideline adherence with AI assistance.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help assess whether AI-generated management plans follow evidence-based recommendations across care stages, regions, and guideline updates.
method: Extract and verify clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations.
Generate scenarios covering diagnosis, investigations, treatment, and complications.
Grade management plans with a clinician-calibrated autorater using a 4-point, severity-based rubric.
evidence_signal: From 436 BMJ Best Practice monographs, researchers generated 3,200 core scenarios; in 200 scenarios evaluated by 9 primary care physicians, AI assistance increased adherence from 50.5% to 70.0%.
watch_item: Guideline adherence in scenario-based testing does not establish improved patient outcomes, and the physician study was small.
paper_title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
